reader.requirement: At --std 85, on a dynamic-access indexed file, READ ... NEXT retrieves the next logical record in the current key of reference: after OPEN the first record; after a READ (format 1 or 2) the first record whose key is greater (or the next duplicate in release order); after START the first record satisfying it; at end 10, and 46 after an unsuccessful READ; a later edition's READ PREVIOUS and a NEXT-less sequential READ are refused at 85. The witness covers prime and alternate keys of reference after OPEN and after a format 2 READ.

edition-consulted.switches: bakes --std (85) into each connector's registration (FileConnector.Edition); no rule of this case reads it except the gates listed
DialectBehavior.IndexedReadPreviousAfterOpenAtEnd, asked only for READ PREVIOUS; a NEXT walk never takes it
DialectBehavior.IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly (02 on a random READ at 85); the FPI it sets for a following NEXT is the same at every edition
VisitReadDirection: READ PREVIOUS is a COBOL-2002 construct, refused at 85 (COBOL0900)
Year < 2002: dynamic READ with AT END and no NEXT refused (COBOL7144, IX.4.5.3 SR5)

reader.edition-search: grep 'Edition|DialectBehavior|Year' over KeyedIoBinder.BindRead, StatementValidation.cs, IndexedConnector.cs and VersionConformancePass.cs
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the NEXT phrase must be written for a dynamic sequential READ (2002+ implies it from AT END) and READ PREVIOUS does not exist; the record a READ NEXT retrieves is the same (p6next printed identical lines at 85 and 2023, p6next-003)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf29_05 covers after OPEN and after a format 2 READ by prime and alternate key; after START, after DELETE/REWRITE/failed WRITE, duplicates in release order, at end then 46, a failed random READ, INTO, variable-length records, LOW-VALUE/HIGH-VALUE keys and the 85-only refusals are not exercised (probed here)

probes.printed: random READ K002 then NEXT K003; DELETE K003 then NEXT K004; REWRITE then NEXT K005; NEXT at end 10 then 46; READ KEY IS alt AA -> K005, NEXT -> K001 (02, duplicate BB follows), K002, K004CCZZ, at end 10; START > K003 then NEXT INTO -> K004CCZZ; failed random READ 23 then NEXT 46; failed WRITE (22) then NEXT from K001 -> K002; keys LOW-VALUES/0000/HIGH-VALUES: NEXT after random READ LOW-VALUES -> ZE, HI, at end 10; RECORD VARYING 6..12: random READ K001 length 07, NEXT K002 length 12
probes.expected: GR4c/d/e selection on the current key of reference (duplicates in release order, 02 when the next record duplicates), GR10 at end 10, GR12 then 46, GR15/GR16 key of reference kept for later format 1 READs, the varying length delivered

probes.printed: --std 85: COBOL0900 READ PREVIOUS requires COBOL-2002; COBOL7144 dynamic READ with AT END and no NEXT (IX.4.5.3 SR5), on both NEXT-less READs; --std 2023 (p6arms-002): compiles clean
probes.expected: 1985 Format 1 has no PREVIOUS, and SR5 requires NEXT for a sequential retrieval in dynamic access

reader.notes: SelectSequentialRecord chooses the rule from the positioner (OPEN/START: >= key; READ: > key plus duplicate ordinal) over the key of reference's tree, matching GR4c-e; ReadRandom sets the FPI and key of reference a following NEXT uses. The 85-specific arms are compile-time (SR5, no PREVIOUS) and both fire.

refuter.evidence: Probe q13next-001 (--std 85): READ K003 then a successful WRITE K004 then NEXT = K004 (GR4d selects by key, not by cursor); random DELETE of the next record K006 then NEXT = K008; REWRITE changing K002's alternate CC->BB places it last among BB duplicates (K001 02, K003 02, K002 00, then K008) and a REWRITE that keeps K001's alternate keeps its place (GR14); START alternate >= CC then NEXT walks the alternate (K008 DD, K004 EE, at end 10); START > K003 (FPI K004), DELETE K004, NEXT = K008 (>= FPI); START > K003 (FPI K008), WRITE K005, NEXT = K008 (IX.4.7.4 GR4a sets the FPI to the record's key, GR4c >= that). Probe q4into-001: after OPEN, READ NEXT INTO TE(XV-N) stores into TE(3), the subscript taken from the record read (GR8b); START on alternate then format 2 READ without KEY makes prime the key of reference for later NEXTs (GR16: K001, K002, K003, at end 10). cite: OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR4c; OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR14 [made available in the same order in which they are released by execution of WRITE statements]; OK §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR4a; OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR8b; OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR13.
